as_told.title: 1971 SALT-era language on coordinating with the Soviets over unknowns

plain: The claim is that in 1971 the United States and the Soviet Union agreed, on paper, to coordinate over unexplained objects, so that neither side would mistake one for an attack. The document is the Agreement on Measures to Reduce the Risk of Outbreak of Nuclear War, signed by the US and the USSR in 1971. Pippa Malmgren, the daughter of the presidential adviser Harald Malmgren, points to it, calling it "the 1971 SALT treaty," after the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks between the two powers. Michels tells it twice in his own words. Once he calls it "the SALT One negotiations, I think it was 1971," and says it is "open source": "we're talking about coordinating with the Russians on the UFO question because we were worried that they'd mistake it for American acts of aggression." In that telling he also brings in John F. Kennedy. The other time he describes it as language "on record" saying "we have to coordinate with the Soviets on unknowns in their airspace." None of the tellers quotes the agreement's own wording. If it is right, the two nuclear powers were treating unknown objects as a real risk of starting a war.
